title: VPC Decision Aid for Compliance Officers
audience: Primary: Compliance officers, security architects, procurement leads. Secondary: Solution engineers and account execs preparing customer briefings.
purpose: Provide short, executable messaging and a decision guide sales can use when engaging regulated buyers evaluating Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) vs hosted alternatives.
background: We see a tranche of finance, healthcare, and government prospects asking for private control planes and proof that control-plane telemetry never touches vendor-managed infrastructure. Sales asks for a concise artifact that: (1) explains our control plane tradeoffs, (2) maps common compliance questions to artifacts we can deliver, and (3) gives objection handling for cost, speed of deployment, and maintenance concerns.
positioning_framework: Core claim: Redwood Private gives regulated teams the predictability of a customer-managed control plane with optional minimal vendor coordination. Emphasize separation of runtime vs control plane, explicit data-plane guarantees, and operator-friendly deployment artifacts (KMS integrations, audit exports, attestation records).
key_messages: Customer-owned control plane: configuration, audit logs, and identity are under customer tenancy in VPC deployments — no vendor-side access by default.
Data-plane isolation: inference workloads and model weights run in customer-controlled subnets; we provide hardened deployment packages for on-prem air-gapped installs.
Short vendor contact surface: we support timeboxed, auditable support sessions with short-lived creds and signed attestation tokens for diagnostics.
Compliance-first integrations: works with enterprise KMS/HSM, optional FIPS-backed crypto, SSO + SCIM, and centralized SIEM log forwarding.
Operational handoff: we provide runbooks, automation templates, and a managed escalation band (level 0–2) so internal teams keep primary operational ownership.
Rollback and fail-safe defaults: automatic fallback to pre-approved safe-model variants and network egress controls to limit surprises during upgrades.
buyer_objections: Objection: "Costs more than hosted — we can’t justify the engineering spend.": Rebuttal: Frame costs as predictable fixed ops (capacity commits or private license) vs unbounded hosted variable spend; highlight unit-cost reductions from colocated GPUs, caching, and batching tuned for their workload. Offer a two-phase approach: pilot on dedicated capacity, then commit to private as usage grows.

Objection: "We don't want another control plane to manage.": Rebuttal: Offer the 'customer-light' mode — customer owns identity, audit, and configs while Redwood provides a narrow admin API for safe upgrades and observability hooks; include templated IaC and a 2-week onboarding package to reduce lift.

Objection: "Vendor can still see metadata / logs.": Rebuttal: Explain explicit log routing (customer SIEM first), log forwarding controls, and artifact-level attestations showing when/if vendor-assisted sessions occurred; provide sample audit export and retention policy examples.

Objection: "On-prem is too slow to stand up in our change window.": Rebuttal: Present an incremental deployment path: VPC-only first (fast), then hybrid (air-gapped components as needed). Provide timeline templates (cloud: 2–4 weeks, hybrid: 6–10 weeks). Offer professional services for accelerated rollout.

Objection: "Security incidents will be hard to coordinate with vendor.": Rebuttal: We publish an incident playbook for private deployments with clear escalation points, signed runbooks, and a configurable EDR integration checklist to ensure cross-team response cadence.

Objection: "We require cryptographic separation (KMS/HSM) and FIPS validation.": Rebuttal: We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSMs and document FIPS-capable configurations; provide a checklist and example HSM policies used in prior customer audits.
competitive_notes: Major cloud providers: sell ease-of-use and low setup friction but retain control plane tenancy and corresponding telemetry access; our angle: match their operational simplicity for day-1 while shifting control and auditability to the customer.

Self-hosted open-source runtimes: offer maximum control but high ops burden; position Redwood Private as 'opinionated self-hosted' — we provide hardened images, prebuilt IaC, and SRE runbooks to reduce time-to-production.

Niche inference vendors: some promise full air-gap but lock in through proprietary appliance form factors; emphasize our flexible deployment models (VPC-first, hybrid, on-prem package) and standard integrations (Terraform, Helm, Ansible).
Key competitive win themes: predictable unit economics, shorter time to compliance artifacts, and smaller vendor blast radius during support engagements.
recommended_playbook_steps: 1) Qualify: Ask about regulatory drivers (e.g., HIPAA, GLBA, FedRAMP), where logs must live, and whether customer-managed KMS/HSM is required.
2) Map artifacts: Commit to deliverables (architecture diagram, KMS integration proof, audit-log export sample, SOC2-like checklist) within the proposal.
3) Pilot: Propose a scoped pilot (4–6 weeks) limited to non-sensitive partitions, delivering a runbook and proof of log separation.
4) Offer PS: Bundle an accelerated onboarding + hardening package as optional professional services to shorten deployment timelines.
5) Contract terms: Include SLOs for control-plane availability in private deployments, support windows, and allowed-attestation language describing vendor access mechanics.

audit-export-sample: 30-days JSON export that maps user actions to tenant IDs
onboarding-checklist: terraform modules, helm charts, and smoke-test commands
attestation-template: signed statement for any vendor-assisted maintenance window
